newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says U.S. rights report exaggerated.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says U.S. rights report exaggerated.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Wednesday a U.S. State Department report accusing Indonesia of serious human rights abuses was exaggerated.
"There are many things in the report which, we believe, have been exaggerated. We will give our response to the report," Alatas, speaking before a cabinet meeting, told reporters without elaborating.
The U.S. State Department said in its annual human rights report on January 30 that Indonesia had continued to commit serious human rights abuses in 1996, including in East Timor.
On East Timor, the report said: "There were further instances of killings, disappearances, torture and excessive use of force by the military and insurgents."
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed the territory the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
The State Department report criticised scores of countries, including Indonesia.

The U.S. report faulted the Indonesian government for continuing "to impose severe limitations on freedom of assembly and association" and said that "in anticipation of the 1997 parliamentary elections, the government took a number of actions to intimidate political opponents".
Indonesia's general election is scheduled for May 29 and the government has banned gatherings ahead of the election to lower the risk of violence.
